chapter: Uptown clubs and the Black Cat
title: Willie Gant as mentor
summary: Greene says Gant was much older, kind, and gave him an education in accompanying singers.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: But, you really -- you got your ABC's then?
Yes. Yes.
[ ] stride piano,
How much older would he have been? Ten years older? He must have been a good bit older?
Oh, yeah. He was much older than I. I don't remember how much, you know.
I take it that you played a pretty big repertoire of music, didn't you?
I had to. You see, I really got an education in the two clubs, more or less, because for the singers you have to -- the singers play in all kinds of keys, you know -- alot of sharps.
Yeah.
You know, each one of them had a different pitch.
And did you have to read music for them?
Well, did he kind of take you under his wing, being an older man, and having been around? In music and longer and all that -- or did it just work itself out?
Well, we just --
It just --
Yeah.
You worked the job --
Yeah, we worked the job, and I think he kind of -- you know -- kind of told me what to do and what not to do, I mean.
Yeah. Was he -- I mean like --
Oh -- he was a beautiful -- beautiful man.
He wasn't like Willie the Lion, I mean he didn't --
Oh, no, no. He didn't go into anything that made me, you know, uncomfortable.
No.
No. No.
Did he sing? Did he sing blues with any of those things?
I don't remember him singing any blues.
Oh, because, you know, alot of piano players did sing --
He must have played -- I mean, he must have played alot of old stuff.
